legacy_projection.route_title: Optimization of Low-High Index Stacking Order (Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass)

route_snapshot.title: Optimization of Low-High Index Stacking Order (Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass)
route_snapshot.scientific_hypothesis: A stacking order with the lower-index material (SiO2) facing the incident medium and the higher-index material (TiO2) adjacent to the glass substrate allows for a broader spectral suppression of reflectance within the 40-160 nm thickness constraints than the reverse order, potentially achieving a mean reflectance below 0.03.
route_snapshot.design_principle: Impedance matching theory suggests stepping the refractive index from air (1.0) to substrate (1.52) via intermediate layers minimizes reflection. Placing SiO2 (1.46) first reduces the large air-to-coating index jump, while TiO2 (2.40) acts as a coupling layer to the substrate. The specific thicknesses will be tuned to create destructive interference across the visible band.
route_snapshot.proposed_topology: Air / SiO2 (variable thickness) / TiO2 (variable thickness) / Glass (n=1.52)
design_variables: thickness of the SiO2 layer (bounded 40-160 nm)
thickness of the TiO2 layer (bounded 40-160 nm)
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm
exactly one layer of each material
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave and non-quarter-wave antireflection coating theory
expected_advantages: Reduced surface reflection due to gradual index transition from air
Potential for broad bandwidth minimization via dual-layer interference
known_risks: The fixed thickness bounds (40-160 nm) may prevent reaching the optimal quarter-wave or half-wave conditions for the entire 450-700 nm band
The specific index combination may not allow a mean reflectance below 0.03 with only two layers
route_snapshot.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) optimization for a planar stack consisting of Air (n=1.0), followed by a SiO2 (Gao) layer (lossless, constant n=1.46), followed by a TiO2 (Siefke) layer (lossless, constant n=2.40), on a semi-infinite Glass substrate (lossless, constant n=1.52). The design variables are the thickness of the SiO2 (Gao) layer and the thickness of the TiO2 (Siefke) layer, both constrained to the range [40, 160] nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence (0 degrees), sampled at 5 nm intervals from 450 nm to 700 nm. Use seed 17 for the optimizer. Allow up to 64 solver evaluations. Report the best found thickness pair, the resulting reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Do not use RCWA, FDFD, or surrogate models.
